audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition financing may break numerator, denominator, and cash-bridge coherence
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,235.178m cash bridge addition, equal to $12.85 per share and 22.6% of $5,476m base equity value; filed acquisition consideration is $2,620m
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds acquisition-financing cash while equity-level OE retains only historical interest expense and the model omits the purchase consideration, target OE and final acquisition financing.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company intends to execute permanent financing, inclusive of the amount to repay the promissory note, using the issuance of long-term debt and common equity, along with expected future free cash flow.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing and perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future risk. The June 2026 cash includes proceeds from $338.4m of net equity issuance and $1,481.2m of net debt issuance, while the numerator remains FY2025 standalone OE. The post-issuance denominator captures issued shares, but the model gives shareholders the financing cash without the corresponding acquisition payment or a coherent post-financing interest burden. The amount is large enough to alter the valuation range materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $1,235.178m cash balance to each financing and use of proceeds, then rerun either a pre-financing standalone case excluding earmarked proceeds and related shares/debt effects, or a probability-weighted acquisition case including $2,620m consideration, target OE, financing interest, integration costs and final diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Upstream abandonment obligations may be an undeducted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest ARO $223.021m, or $2.32 per share; FY2025 settlements $38.862m, equal to 12.9% of the $301.9m anchor; FY2025 estimate revision $56.570m
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured plugging and abandonment cash requirements would reduce normalized OE or require a liability deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has recorded an asset retirement obligation representing plugging and abandonment costs associated with the Integrated Upstream and Gathering segment’s natural gas production wells and has capitalized such costs in property, plant and equipment (i.e. the full cost pool).
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and historical cash settlements are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE maintenance-capital calculation already captures those settlements or how much is regulator-recoverable. A gross bridge deduction alone is only 4.1% of base value, but recurring settlements are meaningful relative to anchor OE. Materiality therefore cannot be established without tracing the existing OE treatment.
audit_findings.action: Trace annual ARO settlements, including the $38.862m FY2025 payment and $56.570m revision, through every OE year; identify the $24.634m regulatory ARO asset and other recoveries; then rerun with either normalized settlement costs in OE or only the unrecovered residual deducted from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Customer-funded removal collections may have been treated as common-equity resources
audit_findings.magnitude: Latest cost-of-removal regulatory liability $319.921m, or $3.33 per share and 5.8% of base value; actual double-counted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer collections may increase cash or historical OE, while future removal expenditures omitted from maintenance capital remain owed to customers rather than available to common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Rather, they are classified as a regulatory liability in recognition of the fact that the Company has collected dollars from customers that will be used in the future to fund asset retirement costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The earmarked regulatory liability is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much of the June cash balance derives from these collections, whether removal spending is already included in OE, or whether rate recovery offsets the spending. The gross liability is large enough to warrant resolution, but it is not itself proof of an equal valuation overstatement.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile removal collections and expenditures by year to depreciation, maintenance capital, regulatory accounting and the cash balance; rerun after eliminating any duplicated cash benefit or deducting only the future removal claim not already represented in OE.

audit_findings.title: Permanent impairments can mechanically inflate later owner earnings through lower depletion
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 after-tax earnings benefit from lower depletion was $7.5m, 2.5% of the $301.9m anchor; treating the entire amount as a recurring anchor adjustment would affect base value by approximately $105m or $1.10 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Impairments lower subsequent depletion expense; because residual D&A remains deducted in OE, lower depletion can raise later OE and influence the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: It should also be noted that a non-cash impairment to write down the book value of the reserves to their present value in any given period causes a reduction in future depletion expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The mechanical effect is demonstrated, but its filed FY2025 scale is small relative to the anchor and valuation. Even the conservative computation treating the full $7.5m as a permanent anchor correction changes the $56.97 base value by about 1.9% and does not change the valuation conclusion. Any larger reserve-replacement deficiency is not established by this finding.
audit_findings.action: Confirm consistent depletion treatment and maintenance-capital coverage before and after the impairments; rerun only if that reconciliation identifies additional impairment-induced OE distortion beyond the filed $7.5m effect.

audit_findings.title: Non-service benefit income may be non-cash earnings from restricted assets
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed FY2025 changes were a $22.4m increase in non-service pension and post-retirement benefit income and a $5.8m contingent-consideration revaluation change; potentially retained amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-cash benefit income or fair-value remeasurement retained in OE would inflate the earnings numerator; regulatory revenue reductions may offset part of the benefit income.
audit_findings.evidence: This increase can be attributed primarily to a $22.4 million increase in non-service pension and post-retirement benefit income combined with a $5.8 million change in the year-over-year revaluation of the contingent consideration received as part of the sale of the Company’s California oil properties in 2022.
audit_findings.explanation: The income changes are demonstrated, but their inclusion in OE is not. The filing also provides a $14m annual Utility revenue reduction intended to match qualified pension and OPEB income, producing zero Utility earnings impact. The record does not allocate the $22.4m change between matched regulated activity and any unmatched amount, or show whether the zero-value contingent consideration was purged. The gross $28.2m change is 9.3% of anchor OE, so the unresolved portion could matter.
audit_findings.action: Inspect each OE-year adjustment for pension, OPEB and contingent-consideration remeasurement; reconcile qualified-plan income to the $14m regulatory revenue offset and remove only unmatched, non-cash amounts before rerunning the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded nonqualified benefits may be missing from the equity claim bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.4m projected benefit obligation, equal to $0.61 per share and 1.1% of $5,476m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual obligation not funded by dedicated assets and not already discharged through OE would be deducted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected benefit obligations for the plans were $58.4 million, $66.0 million and $69.5 million at September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated, but the bridge also excludes the company's other investments, including $44.478m of life-insurance contracts and $13.786m of equity mutual funds at FY2025 that are primarily informal benefit funding. Even deducting the full gross obligation without recognizing any offset reduces base value by only $0.61 per share and does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Match the obligation to legally or economically dedicated insurance and investment assets and to benefit payments already captured in OE; deduct only a verified residual, with no rerun required unless the reconciliation reveals additional omitted claims.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2022 residual D&A $167.4m, equal to 55.4% of the $301.9m anchor; eligible portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A shown by filed evidence to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could raise the log-trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2022 $167.4m (45.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The current treatment is demonstrably conservative because the unidentified amount remains an expense. However, the residual is large relative to anchor OE, so a meaningful eligible portion could change the valuation. The record does not identify that portion or demonstrate that it is economically non-recurring, preventing a materiality determination.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the filed component breakdown for residual D&A in each affected year, classify assets and related maintenance requirements consistently, and rerun the complete OE series and log-trend anchor only for amounts supported as eligible add-backs.
